title: IT-Tools
wrapper_note:
the upstream image starts nginx as root on port 80; TOS forbids root containers,
so this wrapper runs nginx as uid 1000 on port 8080 with pid, temp, log and cache
paths under /tmp. The static files are served from the upstream /usr/share/nginx/html.
wrapper_note_readme: - **Rootless nginx wrapper.** The image starts nginx as root on port 80; `src/entrypoint.sh` starts it as uid 1000 on port 8080 with `/tmp` pid/temp/log paths. The application files are unmodified.
descript: IT-Tools is a collection of handy online tools for developers: token generators, encoders, converters, formatters, network and crypto utilities, and many more. Everything runs in the browser against a static web app, with no account and no server-side data. This package runs the official Docker Hub image as a non-root container.
release_note: 1. First release: IT-Tools 2024.10.22 from Docker Hub, x86_64 + aarch64, non-root.
important: Open the web UI and use the tools directly; there is no login and no persistent data. The app is a static SPA, so the optional /data volume stays empty. Needs DockerEngine; add a registry mirror if Docker Hub is unreachable. Plain HTTP on the LAN; do not expose the published port to the internet without a TLS reverse proxy.

data_notes: IT-Tools is a static single-page application. It has no database, no uploads and no server-side state; the optional `/data` mount is unused and can be ignored.
design_notes: **Rootless nginx.** The upstream nginx runs as root on port 80; `src/entrypoint.sh` runs it as uid 1000 on 8080 with pid/temp/log paths under `/tmp`; the static files are unmodified.
**No persistence.** The app is a static SPA; there is nothing to back up.
**One port.** Only 8080 is published; no privileged mode, no host network, no Docker socket.
limitations: No login and no server-side storage: do not use it for secrets that must be kept on the NAS.
Some browser features (clipboard, file APIs) depend on the browser and on HTTPS; over plain HTTP on the LAN some tools may be limited.
Plain HTTP on the LAN; do not expose the published port to the internet without a TLS reverse proxy.
